prompt: A flat layered paper-cut collage in a strict handcraft design system: everything is cut from colored cardstock and hanji paper with perfectly clean cut edges — NO outline of any kind on any piece: no bright edge line, no white edge, no dark contour line. Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. A premium layered paper-cut illustration, square format. The background is a plain smooth near-white paper sheet (#F4F6F9) with generous calm empty margin. In the middle, a FREE-FORM opening is cut into the paper, its outline designed from the story: shaped like a big billowing plume of steam rising from a black iron porridge cauldron at the bottom of the opening — soft rounded steam curls form the outline. It is NOT a plain circle and NOT a rectangle. The opening is cut through FOUR or FIVE THICK paper layers: each layer is a clearly visible WIDE band following the same outline and stepping inward, colours stepping from pale at the outer edge to deeper and richer toward the centre (cream, soft gold, persimmon orange, red-bean red, deep brick), each layer casting a soft shadow on the next — strong obvious depth like layered paper waves. Inside the deepest layer, a detailed layered paper-cut scene fills the space: an autumn red-bean field and a little thatched cottage under a golden sun, a kind grandmother in hanbok stirring red-bean porridge in a black cauldron, and a chubby cute persimmon-orange tiger cub with dark-brown stripes, cream muzzle and pink cheeks peeking over the inner rim with its paws, curls of paper steam. Story elements break OUT over the outer edge onto the white sheet in a few places: curls of paper steam, a few maple leaves and red beans, and the tiger cub's front paws resting over the lower edge. Most of the white sheet stays empty. Elegant, harmonious, soft light from the top left. Cute Korean picture-book characters for 3-4 year olds, never scary. No text.
